item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
For the first time in a while, no OpenAI model leads the MathArena AI math benchmark. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon and Anthropic's Fable 5.2 have knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top, though both cost significantly more. Gemini ignored the time limit in testing and almost never gave up on a task.

The article Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
Anthropic has made Claude Opus 5.5 the default model on all paid plans and published a guide that does away with old prompting habits. The main takeaway is to drop "think hard" and start at Medium effort.

The article Anthropic says outdated prompting habits are slowing down Claude Opus 5.5 appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
OpenAI is dissolving its standalone robotics team for the second time, but not because it lacks data. General-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can apparently control robots directly, making a dedicated unit unnecessary. The researchers are being redistributed across other teams in what the company frames as a way to accelerate its robotics efforts.

The article OpenAI reassigns robotics researchers to other teams as general-purpose models might make specialized robotics AI unnecessary appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Anthropic can already retrain Mythos with "a fraction of the compute originally needed," says former researcher Coxon
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
Former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon points to a slide from Anthropic's IPO roadshow as a reason he left, saying it shows the company's algorithms are improving not just quickly but at an accelerating rate. Coxon continues to call for a pause on frontier model development so competitors can catch up and human-level AI can become a commodity.

The article Anthropic can already retrain Mythos with "a fraction of the compute originally needed," says former researcher Coxon appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller
item.dc:creator: Tomislav Bezmalinović
item.description:
Runway releases its robotics model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. The model uses knowledge from video training for robot control and leads the World Action Model category on Nvidia's RoboLab-120 benchmark. It can't yet plan complex action sequences on its own, though.

The article Runway's open-source Praxis-1 turns video AI into a robot controller appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
Jensen Huang likely left Nvidia more because of risky business practices than anything else, a Wall Street Journal report suggests. At the very least, those practices made him enemies internally. The company offered cloud providers billions in financial guarantees for chip purchases, including a planned $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Interim CEO and then-CFO Colette Kress tried to contain the risk, and Huang reportedly didn't like that.

The article Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Schreiner
item.description:
OpenAI is taking a second shot at AI-powered shopping with ChatGPT Wallet after scrapping its first approach, Instant Checkout. Users register a card once and confirm each purchase through Face ID or a fingerprint, while actual card details stay hidden behind payment tokens. Rivals such as Anthropic, Meta, and xAI already have their agents making purchases.

The article OpenAI rebuilt AI shopping from scratch with ChatGPT Wallet appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
item.dc:creator: Matthias Bastian
item.description:
Chinese investors are shut out of Anthropic's IPO, Bloomberg reports. Banks are rejecting buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing U.S. export control rules known as ITAR. Similar restrictions applied during SpaceX's IPO, and Anthropic's products aren't available in either region anyway.

The article Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows
item.dc:creator: Manuel Uth
item.description:
Anthropic's new Claude for Manufacturing plugin connects the AI directly to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, and Infor. Its 17 specialized skills let the AI draft quotes, compare suppliers, and place backup orders when deliveries are delayed, all after human approval. The plugin doesn't control physical machines yet, but Anthropic is separately developing the Model Hardware Standard for that.

The article Anthropic's Claude for Manufacturing plugs AI directly into factory software to automate industrial workflows appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails
item.dc:creator: Manuel Uth
item.description:
US public-sector unions are increasingly pushing through protections against AI surveillance and automated firings. In Oakland, a strike vote forced retraining programs instead of layoffs, and a transport union in Ohio won veto power over autonomous vehicles. California banned so-called bossware. All of this is happening while nearly 70 percent of US government agencies already use generative AI.

The article Nearly 70 percent of US agencies use generative AI, and unions are finally catching up with guardrails appeared first on The Decoder.
